claims.claim: The proposal requests 10,000,000 ada, using an approximate USD 0.20 per ada reference rate for an approximately USD 2.0 million planning budget split into two USD 1.0 million pools.

Pool 1 will support protocol infrastructure and staged launch liquidity, deployed over three months in approximate tranches of USD 250,000, USD 250,000, and USD 500,000 after stated readiness, reporting, and performance checks.

Pool 2 will fund delivery, audit, integrations, dashboards, governance reporting, legal/compliance work, and go-to-market execution through itemized planning allocations totaling approximately USD 1.0 million.

Profits, yield, and returns generated by the launch liquidity position will be returned to the Cardano Treasury quarterly, while principal may be returned only after a 30-day time-weighted average TVL of at least USD 60 million and a further governance-approved return action.

Alchemy will use a shared BTC reserve backing FIRE and ICE, with reserve-ratio formulas, a 5.0x initial target reserve ratio, and safety zones that constrain minting and redemption as reserve conditions deteriorate.

FIRE is described as a volatility-absorbing residual BTC-upside asset and ICE as a lower-volatility USD-denominated BTC-backed asset, both intended to circulate as composable Cardano-native primitives.

The proposal asserts that Cardano currently lacks a serious production BTCfi infrastructure layer and risks Bitcoin-backed structured exposure consolidating on Ethereum, BNB, Solana, and off-chain markets if Alchemy is not funded.

The proposal cites Strategy, Strive, Apyx, Saturn, and Pendle as evidence that Bitcoin-backed structured exposure is a real and growing market, with some Strategy and Strive figures tied to referenced external sources.

The proposal identifies BTC volatility, oracle, bridge, Charms protocol-layer, novel asset, delivery, and adoption risks, and proposes mitigations including overcollateralization, audits, modeling, staged launch, dashboards, pause rules, disclosures, fund separation, reporting, and administrator oversight.
Intersect is proposed as interim fund administrator, and administrator-held ada would be kept in auditable accounts and delegated to auto-abstain rather than to a Stake Pool Operator.

Open-source SDKs and adapters for wallets, DEXs, and DeFi protocols
Public dashboards showing reserve ratio, asset supply, liquidity health, fee flows, and deployment status
Monthly governance reports and reporting standards
Independent security review, audit, and economic modeling

0f75dd11be0b7a6cb4b305a175b17cf4b60cd307.message:
BEACN voted NEEDS_MORE_INFO because this is a treasury withdrawal, and a directional vote is blocked until the applicable Net Change Limit is pinned and independently verified from public chain evidence. This is a conservative, evidence-based hold, not a rejection of the idea.

The proposal asks for 10,000,000 ada to fund Alchemy, a Cardano-native Bitcoin treasury protocol and BTCfi infrastructure layer from Sundial Protocol and Charms, with Intersect proposed as an interim fund administrator subject to confirmation and final agreement. It describes a shared BTC reserve, FIRE and ICE assets, SDKs and adapters, public dashboards, monthly reporting, independent security review, audits, economic modeling, legal and compliance work, go-to-market execution, and staged launch liquidity. Several budget and design claims were well supported in the proposal, including the 10,000,000 ada request, the approximate USD 2 million planning budget, the two USD 1 million pools, staged liquidity deployment, reserve-ratio rules, and the planned return of profits, yield, and returns to the Cardano Treasury quarterly.

The review also found important gaps. Some adoption and governance claims were not independently supported, including the claim that Cardano lacks a serious production BTCfi infrastructure layer and risks losing Bitcoin-backed structured exposure to other ecosystems, and the claim about Intersect-administered ada being held in auditable accounts and delegated to auto-abstain rather than to a Stake Pool Operator. Treasury analysis was also missing a sustainability path and clearer cost-benefit case, while the risk review still lacked independent assurance and a dependency map. Execution risk was rated high, and the treasury flow signal was in a stressed regime.

The evidence that would unblock a directional vote is a pinned and independently verifiable Net Change Limit from public chain evidence, plus stronger public evidence for the unsupported adoption and administrator-governance claims, clearer treasury sustainability and cost-benefit analysis, and independent assurance around the main execution and dependency risks. Until then, BEACN cannot justify either a YES or NO without overstating the certainty of the review.

BEACN voted NEEDS_MORE_INFO because this is a treasury withdrawal, and a directional vote is blocked until the applicable Net Change Limit is pinned and independently verified from public chain evidence.

The review found the anchor document was available and replayable, and the strongest YES case was that the proposal substantiates an ecosystem-wide funding mechanism aligned with Vision 2030 KPIs. But treasury actions require elevated scrutiny, claims evidence was thin, execution risk was unknown, and missing items included a line-item budget, sustainability path, independent assurance, dependency map, and verified Net Change Limit evidence. A directional vote would be unblocked by public, replayable evidence for the applicable Net Change Limit and the unsupported operating, treasury, and risk claims.

claims.claim: Hydra is described as the only production-grade Layer 2 on Cardano and a state-channel scaling solution that provides sub-second finality, near-zero fees, high parallel throughput, and L1-grade settlement.
The proposal asks for ₳5,100,781 and says funding will be milestone-gated with independent third-party assurance and Intersect providing administrative treasury governance.

Hydra has powered or is powering applications including Delta DeFi, Masumi, Hydra Doom, Glacier Drop, Intersect voting infrastructure, VTech Labs applications, Blockfrost payments, and Midgard fast withdrawals.

The proposal claims a single Hydra Head processes up to 1,000+ TPS in payment benchmarks and that aggregate throughput scales close to linearly as independent Heads run in parallel.
The proposal claims Hydra uses the same scripts, Plutus, and EUTXO model as Cardano so applications that run on Cardano can run in Hydra unchanged.
The proposal claims Hydra’s custody model requires every participant to sign each state advance, allowing a single honest participant to reclaim funds even if others collude.

The proposal claims Hydra activity can increase Cardano ecosystem activity, TVL, L1 settlement usage, transaction fees, treasury sustainability, and ADA-holder value by retaining high-performance applications on Cardano.
The proposal claims L1 upgrades such as Leios and Peras will strengthen Cardano but cannot provide the zero-fee, sub-second, high-throughput envelope required by high-performance applications.
The proposal says provisional users under evaluation include Bodega Market, Atlas Defi, Wingriders, Houselink, European Public Network, and more.

Maintenance and developer experience work including CI, tooling, and technical debt reduction.

lean.doctrine_basis: Treasury stewardship and downside protection; evidence quality and reproducibility

4f6e5df9a6e14bd49e406e2bbb0d108b3be2be64.message:
BEACN voted ABSTAIN because the review was missing baseline evidence needed to responsibly support or oppose a treasury withdrawal. This is a conservative, evidence-based hold, not a rejection of Hydra v2 or its goals.

The action requested ₳5,100,781 to fund four Hydra v2 workstreams: performance optimization, operational excellence, ecosystem support, and maintenance/developer experience. The proposer claimed Hydra is Cardano’s only production-grade Layer 2, that it can provide sub-second finality, near-zero fees, high throughput, and L1-grade settlement, and that it has powered or is powering several named applications. The proposal did support the basic funding claim, including milestone-gated funding, independent third-party assurance, and Intersect administrative treasury governance. It also supported the claim about Hydra’s custody model requiring every participant to sign each state advance.

The review could not verify several material claims with independent, replayable public evidence, including the production-grade Layer 2 claim, performance claims, adoption claims, and claimed ecosystem impact. Key review gates also remained incomplete or thin: intake was blocked, claims and evidence were thin, treasury analysis was incomplete, and risk review was thin. The review specifically lacked a complete proposal summary, line-item budget, feasibility assessment, risk analysis, alternatives analysis, failure-mode analysis, and community impact analysis.

A directional vote would be unblocked by a complete deep-research dossier with the missing treasury amount field, a line-item budget, evidence for milestone-gated disbursement and independent assurance, independent support for the major technical and adoption claims, and a fuller analysis of feasibility, risks, alternatives, failure modes, and community impact. Until then, BEACN abstained because a treasury action spending shared ADA requires a higher evidentiary bar.

Some governance and economic details were supported in the proposal itself, including the requested amount, the use of USD figures only as planning references, Intersect’s role as fund administrator, gated fund releases, published recommendations and disbursement records, reporting, conflict-of-interest protections, and return triggers. But several important claims still lacked independent evidence, including the core claim that PRIME would improve DeFi readiness, activate incentives responsibly, and grow durable liquidity, and the claim that the withdrawal depends on a valid Net Change Limit with enough remaining capacity at enactment.

This is a conservative, evidence-based hold. The blockers were missing budget analysis and missing feasibility assessment, with additional gaps in line-item budget detail, sustainability path, independent assurance, dependency mapping, and synthesis. A directional vote would require a complete treasury analysis and feasibility review, plus replayable public evidence for the material claims that are currently only proposer-asserted.

claims.claim: Cardano treasury governance is currently in a poor state due to a funding impasse, indirect support in the governance system, and lack of strategic guardrails.
Treasury withdrawal actions from different important domains have created perceived competition for scarce resources and harmful community conflict.
Treasury governance is pivotal for Cardano's growth and stability and should provide clear direction, coherent strategy, and a specific roadmap.
The governance system and constitution should explicitly address and support treasury governance.
The Net Change Limit should not be treated as the overall potential budget because it is only a vague initial approximation and is insufficient alongside incoherent treasury withdrawals.
A dedicated investment budget should include strategic direction, a roadmap, thematic structure, and allocation percentages across domains.
DReps should vote on dedicated balanced budgets rather than directly comparing individual project funding proposals because few DReps have expertise across multiple domains.
A strategic entity should prepare, propose, and implement a budget, and an expert commission should evaluate and select projects that meet budgetary requirements.

The proposed budget structure includes eight domains: core protocol and infrastructure, developer tooling, research and innovation, commercial ecosystem growth, administration and operations, community education and marketing, other strategic or public-good initiatives, and a functional reserve.
AtlasHub is a small DRep committed to Cardano since 2019, with a referenced Cexplorer DRep page.

BEACN voted ABSTAIN because the proposal’s governance-improvement intent was clear, but the evidence threshold was not met for several high-materiality claims. This is a conservative, evidence-based hold, not active opposition.

The action asked to introduce ideas for reforming Cardano treasury governance into public discussion, including guardrails, strategic direction, a possible treasury process built around an NCL vote, budget vote, and withdrawal vote, thematic budgets, and concepts for a strategic entity and expert commission. The proposal did not request a stated treasury amount, name a recipient, or set a deadline.

Some parts were well-supported inside the proposal: the case for a dedicated investment budget with strategic direction, a roadmap, thematic structure, and allocation percentages cleared the evidence gates, and the proposed budget domains were laid out. But several central claims remained proposer assertions rather than independently supported facts, including that treasury governance is currently in a poor state, that different withdrawal actions have created harmful competition and conflict, and that new governance entities are needed to solve those problems.

The review found a pinned, replayable anchor document, so the action could be assessed. But claims-and-evidence review was thin, execution risk was unknown, mitigation evidence and independent assurance were missing, and the flag score reduced confidence. A directional vote would be unblocked by replayable independent evidence for the core dysfunction and conflict claims, plus clearer risk mitigation and assurance for the proposed governance process and entities.

a75645e0871f3dbb6207df867d9bd6a1a3a5befa.message:
BEACN voted ABSTAIN because the proposal raises the Treasury Net Change Limit from 350,000,000 ada to 500,000,000 ada, but the key justification for why that increase is needed was mostly asserted rather than independently evidenced.

The action asked DReps to agree to a fixed 500,000,000 ada Net Change Limit for Cardano Treasury withdrawals during Epochs 613-713. It does not authorize any Treasury Withdrawal, name a recipient, or approve any spending by itself. The proposal clearly states that only enacted Treasury withdrawals debited on-chain count toward the cap, that Treasury inflows do not increase the limit, and that withdrawals already debited in the period count toward the same 500,000,000 ada total.

Several core mechanics were well supported by the proposal document, including the amount, the time period, the accounting treatment, and the fact that this is an InfoAction with no direct on-chain spending effect. The weaker part was the policy case: the claims that the existing 350,000,000 ada limit is becoming constrained, and that raising it preserves room for credible withdrawals while maintaining an appropriate guardrail, were not backed by enough independent evidence. The review also found thin risk evidence, with missing mitigation evidence and independent assurance.

This ABSTAIN is a conservative, evidence-based hold, not active opposition. A directional vote would be unblocked by stronger public evidence showing the current limit is practically constrained, why 500,000,000 ada is the right replacement guardrail for Epochs 613-713, and what mitigations or independent assurance address the governance and execution risks of raising the limit.

fbb8d1a4a8d6b62f8cd706944a0582b884c2b901.message:
BEACN voted NEEDS_MORE_INFO because this treasury request cannot receive a directional vote until the applicable Net Change Limit is pinned and independently verified from public chain evidence. This is a conservative, evidence-based hold, not a rejection of Eternl’s work or a judgment that the request is invalid.

The proposal asks for ₳2,350,000 for 12 months of Eternl operations from August 2026 through July 2027, covering frontend maintenance, backend infrastructure, support, governance tooling, audits, and continued development while paid Pro plans are introduced. The proposal clearly states the requested amount, the approximate $420,000 valuation at $0.1787 per Ada, and the allocation across frontend, backend, support, admin, and audits. It also commits to converting up to $420,000 worth of Ada into stablecoins, using a public company wallet, returning excess Ada above that amount, and performing semiannual repayment checks.

The main weakness is evidence quality on material claims. Several important claims remain proposer-asserted rather than independently evidenced, including the need for 6.0 FTE across 10 contributors at $70,000 per FTE, the claimed install counts, the number of Pro users needed to cover annual costs, the claim that 10-18% of Cardano mainnet transactions use Eternl, and the operational reliability claim. The review also found thin claims-and-evidence support, unknown execution risk, no documented milestone-gated disbursement, missing cost-benefit clarity, missing independent assurance, and no dependency map.

The hold would be unblocked by a pinned and independently verified Net Change Limit from public chain evidence, plus stronger replayable evidence for the key cost, adoption, and operational claims. For a treasury withdrawal of this size, BEACN requires that higher evidence bar before voting YES or NO.

claims.claim: The action upgrades Cardano Mainnet from protocol version 10.0 to protocol version 11.0 without an era transition.
The upgrade introduces new Plutus primitives defined by CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138, and CIP-0153.
All Plutus built-in functions, including newly introduced ones, will become available across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.
UPLC case expressions over Bool, Integer, and Data will provide significant performance improvements and cleaner script logic.
The hard fork promotes VRF key hash uniqueness to a ledger-level rule so no two stake pools can register or operate with the same VRF key.

Testing reports demonstrate no behavioral regressions, complete conformance between specification and implementation for new ledger rules, and correct operation of new Plutus primitives and case expressions across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.
Security audits have been undertaken for Plutus BLS primitives and execution costs for all Plutus primitives.
A linked Cardano Node 11.0.1 performance report shows no regressions for standard value, Plutus, and voting benchmarks and acceptable baseline performance for new primitives and case expressions.
At least 85% of stake pools by active stake should have upgraded to a node version capable of protocol version 11 before ratification, and this must be determined before ratification.

Reversion is only possible in extreme circumstances through the CIP-0135 disaster recovery process, while Plutus primitive use could be disabled by changing companion cost model settings if issues are found.

deliverables: Upgrade Cardano mainnet protocol to major version 11 and minor version 0 while remaining in the Conway era.
Make new Plutus primitives from CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138, and CIP-0153 available.
Make all Plutus built-in functions consistently available across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.
Add UPLC case expressions for Bool, Integer, and Data.
Promote or tighten ledger and node validation, diagnostics, and security rules including VRF key hash uniqueness and PPView mismatch reporting.

fdd468da5cc4ac8431dcd7e2b3211666c73bc229.message:
BEACN voted ABSTAIN because this is a high-impact hard fork, and the review did not find a complete independently pinned readiness packet for protocol readiness, ecosystem readiness, security review, testing, and rollback or containment planning.

The action requested an intra-era hard fork of Cardano mainnet from protocol version 10.0 to 11.0, called the van Rossem hard fork, while staying in the Conway era. The proposal says this would add new Plutus primitives from several CIPs, make Plutus built-in functions consistently available across Plutus V1, V2, and V3, add UPLC case expressions for Bool, Integer, and Data, and tighten ledger and node rules such as VRF key hash uniqueness and PPView mismatch reporting.

Several core claims were reviewable or supported: the protocol version change itself, the linked CIPs for new Plutus primitives, the availability of built-ins across Plutus versions, the VRF uniqueness rule, the 85% active-stake SPO upgrade expectation before ratification, and the linked Cardano Node 11.0.1 performance report. But important readiness claims were still mostly proposer-asserted or thinly evidenced, including no behavioral regressions, full specification-to-implementation conformance, correct operation across Plutus versions, security audits for BLS primitives and execution costs, and performance benefits from UPLC case expressions.

This ABSTAIN is a conservative, evidence-based hold, not a rejection of the upgrade’s goals. A directional vote would be unblocked by a complete independently pinned readiness packet covering version guardrails, testnet results, SPO readiness, exchange readiness, dApp readiness, security review, constitutional alignment, and rollback or containment planning, plus stronger mitigation evidence and independent assurance for the execution risks.

claims.claim: The proposal sets a Net Change Limit of 500,000,000 ada, equal to 500,000,000,000,000 lovelace, for the Cardano Treasury.

Treasury inflows, including reserve and protocol allocations, transaction-fee allocations, refunds, and returns of Treasury-funded amounts, do not count toward or increase the limit.
Treasury Withdrawals already debited during the period count toward the 500,000,000 ada limit and are not reset, reversed, reopened, or reauthorized by this action.
The proposed 500,000,000 ada limit supersedes any prior Net Change Limit for Epochs 613-713, including the previously agreed 350,000,000 ada limit.
The proposal states that the action has no direct on-chain effect and does not authorize any Treasury Withdrawal.

The proposer asserts that the existing 350,000,000 ada limit is becoming practically constrained and that a higher limit preserves DReps' ability to consider credible Treasury Withdrawals on their merits.

gov_action15atytcy8ru7mkcs8m7r8mx7k5x36t.message:
BEACN voted ABSTAIN because the proposal’s core mechanics were clear, but the evidence did not meet the threshold for a directional vote. This is a conservative, evidence-based hold, not active opposition.

The action asked DReps to agree to a new Net Change Limit for the Cardano Treasury for Epochs 613-713, raising the cap to 500,000,000 ada. The proposal stated that this would cap total Treasury Withdrawals debited during that period, would not count Treasury inflows against the limit, would include withdrawals already debited, and would not itself authorize any Treasury Withdrawal. Those points were supported by the pinned, replayable proposal anchor.

The weaker part was the justification for changing the limit. The proposer asserted that the existing 350,000,000 ada limit was becoming practically constrained, and that the new 500,000,000 ada limit would supersede the prior limit for the same period. Those claims were material, but the review found them thinly supported by independent evidence. The risk review was also thin: execution risk was unknown, and mitigation evidence and independent assurance were missing.

For BEACN to move from ABSTAIN to a directional vote, the review would need stronger replayable evidence that the new limit validly supersedes the prior 350,000,000 ada limit, independent support for why the higher limit is needed, and clearer risk mitigation or assurance. Until then, abstaining avoids overstating confidence while still recognizing that the proposal’s basic requested cap and accounting rules were clearly presented.

claims.claim: The proposal changes the minimum Constitutional Committee size parameter, committeeMinSize, from 7 to 5.

If Constitutional Committee membership drops below committeeMinSize, governance actions requiring Constitutional Committee approval become ineligible for ratification, including Parameter Changes, Constitution Updates, Treasury Withdrawals, and Hard Forks.

The document states the change satisfies guardrails requiring committeeMinSize to be non-negative, at least 3, and no more than 10.

claims.claim: The action proposes upgrading Cardano mainnet from protocol version 10.0 to 11.0 through an intra-era hard fork that remains in the Conway era.

The upgrade adds new Plutus primitives defined in CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138 and CIP-0153, including modular exponentiation, dropList, BLS12-381 multi-scalar multiplication, Array, and Value-related built-ins.
The proposal states that all Plutus built-in functions, including newly introduced ones, will become available across Plutus V1, V2 and V3.
The proposal claims native case expressions over Bool, Integer and Data in Untyped Plutus Core will provide significant performance gains and cleaner script logic.

The proposal states that testing reports demonstrate no behavioral regressions, complete conformance between specification and implementation for new ledger rules, and correct operation of the new Plutus primitives and case expressions across Plutus V1, V2 and V3.

The proposal links to Cardano Node 11.0.1 performance results that it says show no regressions for standard value, Plutus and voting benchmarks, and acceptable baseline performance for new Plutus primitives and case expressions.
The proposal states that security audits have been undertaken for Plutus BLS primitives and execution costs for all Plutus primitives.

The proposal says at least 85% of stake pools by active stake should have upgraded to a node version capable of supporting protocol version 11 before ratification, and that this readiness must still be determined prior to ratification.
The proposal claims the governance action is consistent with all eight listed Cardano Constitution hard fork guardrails, provided attention is paid to HARDFORK-04 stake pool readiness.

The proposal states that reversion is only possible in extreme circumstances through the CIP-0135 disaster recovery process, while Plutus primitive use could be disabled by changing companion cost model settings if issues are discovered.
